text: # CTCAE v5.0 Organ Toxicity Grading Reference ## Category: Toxicity & Adverse Event Severity ### 1. General Severity Scale - **Grade 1 (Mild)**: Asymptomatic or mild symptoms; clinical or diagnostic observations only; intervention not indicated. - **Grade 2 (Moderate)**: Minimal, local or noninvasive intervention indicated; limiting age-appropriate instrumental Activities of Daily Living (ADL). - **Grade 3 (Severe)**: Severe or medically significant but not immediately life-threatening; hospitalization or prolongation of hospitalization indicated; disabling; limiting self-care ADL. - **Grade 4 (Life-threatening)**: Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention indicated. - **Grade 5 (Death)**: Death related to adverse event. ### 2. Organ-Specific CTCAE Grading Definitions - **Hematologic (Neutropenia)**: - Grade 1: LLN - 1500 /mm3 - Grade 2: < 1500 - 1000 /mm3 - Grade 3: < 1000 - 500 /mm3 - Grade 4: < 500 /mm3 (Febrile Neutropenia requires immediate emergency hospitalization) - **Hepatic (ALT / AST Elevation)**: - Grade 1: > ULN - 3.0x

< 1000 - 500 /mm3 - Grade 4: < 500 /mm3 (Febrile Neutropenia requires immediate emergency hospitalization) - **Hepatic (ALT / AST Elevation)**: - Grade 1: > ULN - 3.0x ULN - Grade 2: > 3.0 - 5.0x ULN - Grade 3: > 5.0 - 20.0x ULN - Grade 4: > 20.0x ULN - **Renal (Creatinine Elevation)**: - Grade 1: > 1.5 - 2.0x baseline - Grade 2: > 2.0 - 3.0x baseline - Grade 3: > 3.0x baseline or > 4.0 mg/dL - Grade 4: Life-threatening consequences; dialysis indicated - **Pulmonary (Pneumonitis)**: - Grade 1: Asymptomatic, radiographic findings only - Grade 2: Symptomatic, medical intervention indicated (corticosteroids) - Grade 3: Severe symptoms, oxygen indicated - Grade 4: Life-threatening respiratory compromise, intubation indicated
